Middle East.headline: Red Sea/Yemen — Houthi missile attack on cargo ship kills six
Middle East.body: An attack attributed to Iran-backed Houthi rebels targeted the food-carrying cargo ship Tihamah in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, according to Yemen's Ministry of Transport. An initial missile strike sparked a fire, followed by a second strike during search and rescue operations. At least six people were killed, including four crew members—three Pakistani nationals and one Indonesian—and two Yemeni rescue workers, with five others injured. Separately, the U.S. military disabled a vessel near the Gulf of Oman, while Iranian officials warned of potential closures at the Strait of Hormuz unless political and economic conditions are met.

Middle East.headline: Gaza — Israeli drone strike targets vehicle near Abu Asi shelter camp
Middle East.body: An Israeli drone strike destroyed a vehicle immediately adjacent to the Abu Asi Orphan Camp shelter in Al Bureij, central Gaza. The attack targeted a vehicle belonging to an individual supporting displaced children and families in the camp. Despite sustaining injuries in the strike, local personnel continued providing care and assistance to displaced civilians residing at the shelter site.

Middle East.headline: Syria — Attack on military position in Qamishli leaves two dead
Middle East.body: An attack by an unidentified group targeted a position of the Syrian army's Qamishli Brigade in Tawil Harb village, rural Qamishli, northeast Syria. According to a military spokesperson, two fighters were killed and two others were wounded in the assault. The brigade comprises integrated members of the Syrian Democratic Forces. Operations remain ongoing to locate those involved.

Middle East.headline: Yemen — U.S. Defense Department reports 153 civilian deaths from strikes
Middle East.body: A Defense Department report submitted to the U.S. Congress disclosed that American military strikes in Yemen resulted in 153 civilian deaths over the past year. The report specified that 15 separate military strikes are currently undergoing internal investigation regarding civilian casualties.

Americas.headline: Colombia — 7.4-magnitude earthquake kills hundreds and causes widespread destruction
Americas.body: A 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia near San Jose del Palmar in Chocó department, causing extensive damage across major urban centers including Cali, Pereira, Quibdó, Manizales, and Armenia. Authorities placed affected cities under red alert as collapsed buildings trapped residents and disrupted critical infrastructure. Seven airports suspended operations alongside disruptions to energy, telecommunications, aqueducts, and transportation networks. Search and rescue operations remain underway as rescuers search through rubble for survivors. At least 240 fatalities have been confirmed, with widespread destruction leaving many residents homeless.

Americas.headline: Venezuela — Official death toll from twin earthquakes reaches 6,301
Americas.body: The official death toll from two major earthquakes that struck Venezuela on June 24 has reached 6,301 following the confirmation of 176 additional fatalities. The twin tremors, measuring 7.2 and 7.5 in magnitude, hit La Guaira state and the Caracas metropolitan area hardest, representing the country's most devastating seismic event in recent history. Parliamentary officials reported that 73,356 individuals have received medical treatment since the disaster, while authorities continue damage assessments on tens of thousands of affected structures.

Africa.headline: DR Congo — Rapidly accelerating Ebola outbreak surpasses 2,000 deaths
Africa.body: An unprecedented Ebola virus outbreak in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed more than 2,000 people, making it the fastest-spreading outbreak on record. Health officials report at least 4,381 confirmed cases across five provinces, driven by the rare Bundibugyo strain for which no approved vaccines or treatments exist. World Health Organization officials revealed the outbreak began in February, months before its official declaration in May. Containment operations are severely hindered by ongoing local conflict, health worker strikes over unpaid wages, widespread misinformation, and cuts to international aid. Cases continue to double in some hotspots, prompting calls for an immediate global response scale-up.

Europe.headline: Russia/Ukraine — Cross-border attacks kill four and damage infrastructure
Europe.body: Overnight cross-border strikes across southern Russia and Ukraine resulted in at least four fatalities. In the Russian port city of Novorossiysk, local officials reported that a child was among those killed, while dozens of buildings sustained physical damage during the overnight attacks. The strikes reflect ongoing military action directly impacting civilian populations and residential infrastructure on both sides of the border.

Europe.headline: Ukraine — Human Rights Watch warns against retransfer of outdated cluster munitions
Europe.body: Human Rights Watch has urged the United States to reject a request from Türkiye to retransfer tens of thousands of stockpiled cluster munitions to Ukraine. The rights group warned that transferring obsolete munitions manufactured over 30 years ago creates severe, foreseeable humanitarian risks for civilians due to their inaccuracy and unreliability. More than 110 nations have banned cluster munitions under international treaties due to the long-term threat posed to civilian populations.

Europe.headline: Ukraine — Alleged North Korean missile strike hits Zaporizhzhia
Europe.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused North Korea of increasing military support to Russia following a deadly attack on Zaporizhzhia reportedly conducted using Pyongyang-supplied ballistic missiles. The strike on Zaporizhzhia highlights ongoing threats to civilian centers from long-range weapon systems. Following the development, Ukrainian officials are actively seeking closer cooperation with South Korea.
verified_figures: Deadly missile attack reported in Zaporizhzhia

Asia-Pacific.headline: Myanmar — Military escalates aerial attacks on civilians using low-cost aircraft
Asia-Pacific.body: A United Nations investigation reported that Myanmar's military has escalated aerial attacks against civilians by increasingly using low-cost aircraft, including motorized paragliders and gyrocopters, in its conflict with anti-government armed groups. Separately, the Arakan Army ethnic armed group reported that military strikes in Rakhine state have killed 20 civilians so far this month. The military government did not immediately respond to the report or allegations, though it has previously stated it only targets legitimate military objectives.

Asia-Pacific.headline: China — Typhoon Dolphin remnants cause mass evacuations in Beijing
Asia-Pacific.body: Remnants of Typhoon Dolphin brought torrential rain across northern and central China, triggering mass evacuations in Beijing due to severe flood and landslide risks. Forecasters warned that parts of the capital could receive between 150mm and 200mm of rain over 24 hours, equal to more than one-third of the city's average annual precipitation. Heavy rainfall has disrupted roads, construction sites, and regional infrastructure across affected areas.
verified_figures: 150mm to 200mm of rainfall forecast over 24 hours

Asia-Pacific.headline: India — Severe monsoon flooding inundates villages in Assam state
Asia-Pacific.body: Severe monsoon flooding inundated communities in the Sivasagar district of India's northeastern Assam state, submerging homes and damaging local infrastructure. In affected locations like Charing village, residents were forced to construct makeshift banana log rafts to evacuate elderly and immobile family members due to an absence of official rescue teams and boats. Displaced residents have sought safety in makeshift shelter camps established along national highways.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Ebola deaths surge past 2,000 – as outbreak spread for months undetected
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: More than 2,000 people have now died of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), with the outbreak continuing to outpace the response because it spread for months undetected before being declared. Government data shows the outbreak has recorded a total of 4,381 confirmed cases. The ongoing outbreak has so far had a case fatality rate of 45.9 per cent, more than the 39.6 per cent rate recorded in the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak, which infected more than 28,000 people and killed at least 11,000. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Ebola deaths top 2,000 as scientists race to develop vaccine
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Ebola deaths top 2,000 as scientists race to develop vaccine The current Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo species, was declared by DRC health officials on 15 May and declared a public health emergency of international concern by the World Health Organization (WHO) two days later. With more than 4,000 confirmed cases, it is both the second-largest and the fastest-growing on record. Only West Africa’s 2014 to 2016 outbreak, which saw more than 11,000 deaths, was larger. Just three months into this Ebola emergency, the death toll is already close to the total number of people killed in the 2018 to 2020 epidemic, which saw fewer overall cases.
